database_summary: Small mixed dataset containing: (1) a pizza ordering domain (customers orders, cleaned orders, runners, runner orders, recipes, toppings, extras/exclusions lookup tables, pizza names) that records order events and some lookup/descriptor tables; (2) company funding and dates/industry tables (company descriptors and snapshot funding values); (3) large NYC trees and related income by zipcode and public-health-like statistics and a large word list. The schema mixes event-level rows (orders, runner events, statistics over time) with descriptive/dimensional rows (pizza_names, pizza_toppings, pizza_recipes, companies_dates, companies_industries) and measured spatial rows (trees). Joins between recipe/topping mapping and orders require careful handling because recipe.toppings is a delimited string (not normalized).

accepted.name: clean_runner_orders_numeric
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  runner_id,
  pickup_time,
  distance AS distance,
  duration AS duration,
  cancellation
FROM pizza_clean_runner_orders
UNION ALL
SELECT
  order_id,
  runner_id,
  pickup_time,
  CAST(NULLIF(REPLACE(REPLACE(distance,'km',''), ' ', ''), '') AS REAL) AS distance,
  -- remove REGEXP_REPLACE; strip non-numeric chars by chaining common replacements and fallback to NULL if empty
  CAST(NULLIF(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(duration, 'h', '.'), 'm', ''), ' ', ''), '') AS REAL) AS duration,
  cancellation
FROM pizza_runner_orders
WHERE distance IS NOT NULL OR duration IS NOT NULL

semantic_filters.cancellation: IS NULL OR cancellation IS NOT NULL

accepted.description: Normalized runner order events with numeric distance and duration. Use when queries need consistent numeric measures for distance/duration and to prefer cleaned numeric source but fall back to parsing textual fields when only text exists. | Use for: Compare average/median runner distance or duration; Identify slow deliveries or outlier durations; Join runner performance to orders/customers

accepted.name: orders_with_pizza_and_customer_clean
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  pcco.order_id,
  pcco.customer_id,
  pcco.pizza_id,
  pn.pizza_name,
  pcco.exclusions,
  pcco.extras,
  pcco.order_time
FROM pizza_clean_customer_orders pcco
LEFT JOIN pizza_names pn ON pn.pizza_id = pcco.pizza_id
accepted.description: Denormalized cleaned customer orders joined to pizza name. One row per cleaned order. Useful for order-level reporting with pizza descriptive attributes. | Use for: Order counts by pizza_name over time; Customer-level purchase history; Filter orders by presence of extras/exclusions

accepted.name: pizza_recipe_topping_expansion
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  pizza_id,
  CAST(trim(value) AS INTEGER) AS topping_id
FROM (
  SELECT
    pizza_id,
    -- split by comma into rows using recursive CTE pattern emulation via json_each workaround
    -- wrap toppings as JSON array by replacing commas with '","' and surrounding with [""]
    -- then use json_each to unnest. If toppings is NULL or empty, no rows produced.
    replace(replace('[' || '"' || replace(toppings, ',', '","') || '"' || ']', '""', '"') , '[""]', '[]') AS toppings_json
  FROM pizza_recipes
) pr, json_each(pr.toppings_json)
WHERE value <> ''
accepted.description: Explodes pizza_recipes.toppings delimited list into one row per (pizza_id, topping_id) for joining to pizza_toppings. Useful when analyzing topping popularity per pizza. Assumes toppings are comma-separated integers in the toppings text. | Use for: Count how often each topping appears across pizzas; Join to pizza_toppings to get topping_name per pizza; Find pizzas containing a particular topping_id

accepted.name: pizza_toppings_with_names
accepted.description: Simple pass-through of toppings lookup. Use when queries need topping_name by topping_id. | Use for: Lookup topping_name for display or joins; Aggregate topping usage with readable names

accepted.name: orders_with_runner_metrics
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  o.customer_id,
  o.pizza_id,
  o.order_time,
  r.runner_id,
  r.pickup_time AS runner_pickup_time,
  r.distance AS runner_distance,
  r.duration AS runner_duration,
  r.cancellation AS runner_cancellation
FROM pizza_clean_customer_orders o
LEFT JOIN clean_runner_orders_numeric r ON r.order_id = o.order_id
accepted.description: One row per order enriched with runner numeric metrics when available (distance/duration) by left-joining the normalized runner orders. Useful for combining order-level info with delivery performance. | Use for: Assess delivery time vs order time; Compute average delivery duration per pizza or customer; Identify cancelled deliveries

accepted.name: company_funding_summary_by_company
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  company_id,
  MAX(valuation) AS valuation,
  MAX(funding) AS funding
FROM companies_funding
GROUP BY company_id
accepted.description: Aggregated funding snapshot per company_id exposing total funding and valuation measures. Useful as a stable source of company-level funding metrics. | Use for: Rank companies by valuation or funding; Join company financials to dates or industries

accepted.name: companies_with_industry_and_dates
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  cd.company_id,
  cd.date_joined,
  cd.year_founded,
  ci.industry
FROM companies_dates cd
LEFT JOIN companies_industries ci ON ci.company_id = cd.company_id
accepted.description: Denormalized company descriptor: one row per company_id with founding year, joinable industry. Use for company-level cohorts and time-based analyses. | Use for: Cohort companies by year_founded; Aggregate funding by industry and founding year

accepted.name: trees_by_ntaname
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  nta_name,
  boroname,
  borocode,
  state,
  COUNT(*) AS tree_count,
  AVG(tree_dbh) AS avg_tree_dbh,
  SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'Alive' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS alive_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN health = 'Good' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS good_health_count
FROM trees
GROUP BY nta_name, boroname, borocode, state
accepted.description: Aggregated tree counts and basic health summary per NTA (neighborhood). One row per nta_name with counts and average dbh. Useful for spatial neighborhood-level tree reporting and joins to income by zipcode. | Use for: Compare tree density across neighborhoods; Relate neighborhood tree health to income or zipcode-level metrics

accepted.name: income_by_zipcode
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  zipcode,
  Estimate_Total,
  Margin_of_Error_Total,
  Estimate_Median_income,
  Margin_of_Error_Median_income,
  Estimate_Mean_income,
  Margin_of_Error_Mean_income
FROM income_trees
accepted.description: Pass-through of income estimates per zipcode with preserved original column names. Use when joining socioeconomic data to spatial features like trees. | Use for: Join income to trees by zipcode; Analyze median income vs tree_count

accepted.name: latest_statistics_per_state
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  date,
  state,
  total_cases,
  total_deaths,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY state ORDER BY date DESC) AS date_rank
FROM statistics
accepted.description: Latest statistics row per state based on date. Exposes a state-level latest flag and rank for selecting most recent snapshot per state. | Use for: Select the latest statistics per state (WHERE date_rank = 1); Trend analyses using per-state time series
